businessRules.rule: Any report may be printed. Any report presenting a list may be downloaded as a spreadsheet, and any report may be downloaded as a PDF — the spreadsheet for a list somebody will filter and sort afterwards, and the PDF for anything that will be signed, filed or sent unaltered.

An export carries exactly the rows and the columns the user could see on screen and nothing further. A report the user may read and a file the user may take are the same data under the same restrictions, so the export applies the salary rule, which hides the salary section from the School Admin on every list, report and export; the sealed branch boundary, so that a report never crosses into a branch the user cannot open; and every other field restriction in the system. An export built from the underlying query rather than from what was shown on screen will return restricted columns and must not be built that way.

Every export is written to the audit log with the user, the report, the parameters it was run with, the format taken and the number of rows, because a spreadsheet of every guardian's phone number or every student's identity number leaves the system and is not seen again.

Downloading is not a permission of its own. Whoever may view a report may print it and download it, because a person who can already read every row on screen is not stopped from keeping them by withholding a button. What controls exposure is who may open the report at all, and the field restrictions.

Every printed or exported file carries a header naming the school and branch, the report, the parameters it was run with, the date and time it was run and the user who ran it, since a spreadsheet with no context circulates for months and nobody can later say what it shows.
Reports are branch-scoped. The School Admin and the Principal read and download every report of their own branch, and no report of any other.
The Super Admin reads and downloads the reports of every branch, each branch on its own.

The Super Admin alone can also run a report across all branches at once, as one combined report rather than one report per branch. This applies to every report in the catalogue, and it matters most for finance: collection, cash book, outstanding and defaulters, invoices and receipts, concessions and write-offs, the general ledger, the trial balance, income and expenditure, and budget against actual can all be run as a single set of figures for the whole group, so that the school reads its finances as one rather than assembling them by hand from each campus.

A combined report exists only for the Super Admin. Nobody else can run it, open it, or be given it, because the moment one branch's figures sit beside another's they are outside the sealed branch boundary every other role is held to. A Principal or School Admin who needs a group figure asks the Super Admin for it; they cannot produce it themselves and cannot be granted the right to.

This states once, for every report in this section and every list elsewhere in the system, how a report may be taken away, who may take it, and how far it reaches across branches, rather than repeating it on each report.

departures.aspect: Built from the screen, never the query
departures.requirement: Every export is constructed from the rows and columns that were shown. There is no code path that exports from the underlying query, because such a path returns restricted columns.

departures.aspect: The file and the screen are the same data
departures.requirement: Every field restriction that applies on screen applies to the file — the salary rule, the branch boundary and all others.
An export that cannot be written to the audit log does not complete, because a file that leaves the system unrecorded is never seen again.
Every printed or exported file carries its context, since a spreadsheet with none circulates for months and nobody can say what it shows.

departures.aspect: Combined is the Super Admin's alone
departures.requirement: A report combining branches cannot be run, opened or granted to any other role by any route. This settles for reports the question left open about who sees consolidated figures.
Export records are retained 7 years, since they explain what left the system and when.

openQuestions.question: This says a combined report cannot be granted to anybody, while the branch use case says the Super Admin may grant a named Principal or Director a consolidated view. The two cannot both hold, and this feature states that it settles the question for reports.

conventionsApplied.name: session-and-authentication
conventionsApplied.rule: Every use case except the login use case assumes an authenticated session. Sign out is available on every screen. An expired or invalid session returns the user to the login screen with the message "Your session has ended. Please sign in again."

conventionsApplied.name: role-based-access
conventionsApplied.rule: Access is enforced server-side on every request, not only by hiding menu items. A request for a record outside the actor's permitted scope returns a 403 and the message "You do not have permission to view this record." A use case states additions and restrictions only.

conventionsApplied.name: branch-scope
conventionsApplied.rule: Every record carries a branch ID. Users see only their own branch unless the use case states otherwise. Super Admin, School Admin and Principal may switch branch from the header.

conventionsApplied.name: list-screens
conventionsApplied.rule: Every list supports search, column sort and page-size selection. Default page size 25; default sort is most recent first. Filters are applied before printing or exporting.

conventionsApplied.name: print-and-pdf
conventionsApplied.rule: Every report and list offers Print and Download as PDF, honouring the filters currently applied. Each output carries the school name, branch, academic session, report title, filter summary, generation timestamp and the name of the user who generated it.

conventionsApplied.name: audit-trail
conventionsApplied.rule: Every create, update, deactivation, approval and reversal writes to the audit log: actor, role, timestamp, record type, record ID, before and after values, and IP address. Audit entries are never editable.

conventionsApplied.name: validation-and-messages
conventionsApplied.rule: Field-level errors appear inline beneath the field on blur and on submit. Errors that block the whole action appear as a banner at the top of the form. Successful actions show a toast. No action succeeds silently.

conventionsApplied.name: dates-times-numbers
conventionsApplied.rule: Dates display as DD-MM-YYYY; date and time as DD-MM-YYYY HH:mm in 24-hour form. Times are school-local. Phone numbers are stored in the registered mobile format.

conventionsApplied.name: language
conventionsApplied.rule: All user-visible strings come from a resource file. No hard-coded text in any screen.

conventionsApplied.name: screen-states
conventionsApplied.rule: Every list, dashboard tile and report defines four states: loading, empty, error and populated. The empty state names what is missing and links to the action that creates it.

conventionsApplied.name: default-performance-and-retention
conventionsApplied.rule: Unless a use case states otherwise: a screen loads within 2 seconds and a save completes within 2 seconds at 200 concurrent users; lists paginate above 100 rows; financial and student records are retained 7 years; audit and message logs 12 months; every screen is usable at a 360 px viewport. Fill the non-functional field only to depart from this.

conventionsApplied.name: default-trigger
conventionsApplied.rule: Unless a use case states otherwise, the trigger is: the user navigates to the screen and initiates the action. Fill the Triggers field only where a scheduled job, an event in another module, or an inbound external call also starts it.
